title: Housing is becoming an integration and participation infrastructure: affordability, neighbourhoods and legal status shape who can belong and advance
source_unit: Expert Council on Integration and Migration, Room for Development: Housing and Participation in an Immigration Society, Annual Report 2026
geography: Germany, with national and urban-neighbourhood comparisons involving people with and without a migration background

observations.period: 2026 annual report; housing and migration conditions

demand_supply.value: housing demand is growing while supply stagnates in many German cities, making affordable access difficult for people entering or moving within the housing market

group_difference.value: people with a migration background are disproportionately represented among low-income individuals and families facing housing difficulty

participation_link.value: housing conditions affect integration and participation, including access to labour markets, education and local social infrastructure

observations.method: Scientifically based annual report combining housing, migration, settlement, neighbourhood and participation analysis with policy recommendations.
observations.uncertainty: The public summary establishes structural associations and policy pathways; it does not provide a single causal estimate of housing on integration or participation outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Immigrants, descendants of immigrants, low-income households, families, international workers, refugees, local residents and municipalities.
observations.counterinterpretation: Housing matters for participation, but labour-market access, legal status, discrimination, school quality, transport, language, health and social networks also shape outcomes.

observations.period: 2026 annual report; regional distribution and tenure

denominator.unit: Germany-wide population distribution and tenure comparison

regional_distribution.value: people with a migration background are unevenly distributed, with higher population shares in city-states and former western industrial centres and lower shares in eastern federal states

tenure.value: people with a migration background are more likely to rent and less likely to own than people without one, with movement toward parity associated with longer residence and the second generation

context.value: regional differences are linked to reasons for migration, entry period and legal-framework conditions

observations.method: Comparative analysis of settlement patterns, housing tenure and migration-background groups across German regions and generations.
observations.uncertainty: The patterns describe population distributions and associations; they do not isolate the effects of migration background from income, age, household composition, discrimination, market timing or legal status.
observations.subgroup: First-generation immigrants, second-generation residents, renters, homeowners, city-state residents, western industrial regions and eastern federal states.
observations.counterinterpretation: Greater renting can reflect age, arrival timing and life-cycle position rather than a permanent exclusion from ownership or local belonging.

observations.period: 2026 annual report; neighbourhoods, segregation and social interaction

arrival_places.value: neighbourhoods with many migrants do not automatically hinder integration and can provide important resources for newly arrived people

poverty_entanglement.value: where poverty and immigration overlap, residents' participation chances and social coexistence can be weakened

segregation.value: ethnic segregation is low by international comparison and decreasing overall, while income-based social segregation has increased

observations.method: Neighbourhood and urban analysis distinguishing ethnic concentration, income segregation, local social infrastructure and participation conditions.
observations.uncertainty: Neighbourhood composition is not itself a causal treatment; the report does not imply that diversity, poverty or migration has one uniform effect across places.
observations.subgroup: Newly arrived migrants, long-term residents, low-income households, children and young people, local institutions and residents of arrival neighbourhoods.
observations.counterinterpretation: Arrival neighbourhoods can provide social networks and services, but concentrated disadvantage may still reduce opportunity when housing, transport, education and local investment are inadequate.

observations.period: 2026 annual report; skilled workers and refugee housing constraints

denominator.unit: report pathways for international skilled workers and refugees

skilled_worker_access.value: lack of affordable housing can hinder recruitment and retention of international skilled workers needed amid demographic change

housing_discrimination.value: half of international skilled workers report experiencing discrimination in the housing market

refugee_choice.value: refugees generally have limited choice over where and how they are housed during asylum processing and may remain subject to residence restrictions after recognition

observations.method: Synthesis of housing, labour-market, migration-management and legal-administrative evidence with policy recommendations.
observations.uncertainty: The public page does not provide the full survey design or causal estimate behind the skilled-worker discrimination figure; legal rules and local implementation can vary by status and exception.
observations.subgroup: International skilled workers, refugees and asylum seekers, employers, housing associations, municipalities and local residents.
observations.counterinterpretation: Employer-supported housing and local investment may reduce recruitment barriers, but they can also create dependence on employers or concentrate workers in specific areas.

boundary: This record adds a housing-to-participation route in an immigration society, linking affordability, tenure, migration status, neighbourhood resources, poverty, segregation, local infrastructure, labour-market access, discrimination and legal choice. It is a Germany-specific annual report and public summary, not a U.S. housing estimate, respondent-level longitudinal dataset, causal neighbourhood experiment or proof that any recommendation has been implemented.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official SVR English annual-report page was reviewed for the housing and migration frame, regional distribution, tenure, neighbourhood participation, segregation, skilled-worker housing and refugee accommodation findings.
